Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [ˈsen.tɾu]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic, Valencia) [ˈsen.tɾo]

Verb

[edit]

centro

  1. first-person singular present indicative of centrar

  • Audio 2:(file)

centro (accusative singular centron, plural centroj, accusative plural centrojn)

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin centrum, from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron, “sharp point”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈθentɾo/ [ˈθen̪.t̪ɾʊ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ˈθentɾo/ [ˈθen̪.t̪ɾʊ]
  • IPA(key): (seseo) /ˈsentɾo/ [ˈsen̪.t̪ɾʊ]

  • Rhymes: -entɾo
  • Hyphenation: cen‧tro

Noun

[edit]

centro m (plural centros)

  1. centre
  2. downtown

Derived terms

[edit]
  • centrismo
  • centrista

Related terms

[edit]
  • central

Further reading

[edit]
  • “centro”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026

Ido

[edit]

Pronunciation

Noun

[edit]

centro (plural centri)

  1. center (US), centre (UK)

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (standard, Tuscany) IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃɛn.tro/
    • Rhymes: -ɛntro
    • Hyphenation: cèn‧tro
  • (central Italian, Romanesco) IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃen.tro/[1]
    • Rhymes: -entro
    • Hyphenation: cén‧tro

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin centrum, from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron, “sharp point”). The nonstandard pronunciation with -é- might be due to influence of entrare.

Noun

[edit]

centro m (plural centri)

  1. centre, center
  2. middle, midpoint
  3. core, heart
  4. city centre/city center, downtown

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsẽ.tɾu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsẽ.tɾu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsẽ.tɾo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈsẽ.tɾu/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ẽtɾu
  • Hyphenation: cen‧tro

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin centrum (“centre”), from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron, “sharp point”), from κεντέω (kentéō, “to sting”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱent-.

Noun

[edit]

centro m (plural centros)

  1. centre (middle of anything)
    Synonym: meio
  2. center (point on a line midway between the ends)
  3. downtown
    Synonym: baixa
  4. (Brazil, Umbanda) An Umbanda house of worship or temple
    Synonym: terreiro
Derived terms
[edit]
  • centrão
  • centrismo
  • centrista
Related terms
[edit]
  • central
  • centralizar
  • centrar

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

centro

  1. first-person singular present indicative of centrar

[edit]
  • “centro”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “centro”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
centro
Wikipedia es

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈθentɾo/ [ˈθẽn̪.t̪ɾo] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /ˈsentɾo/ [ˈsẽn̪.t̪ɾo] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -entɾo
  • Syllabification: cen‧tro

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin centrum,[1] from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron, “sharp point”), from κεντέω (kentéō, “to sting”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱent-.

Noun

[edit]

centro m (plural centros)

  1. (general) center
  2. (geometry) center
  3. (politics) center, moderate tendencies or ideas
  4. middle
  5. core, heart
    Synonym: medio
  6. (urban studies) city center, downtown
  7. (soccer) cross (a pass in which the ball travels from by one touchline across the pitch)
Derived terms
[edit]
  • centrar
  • centrismo
  • centrista
  • centro comercial
  • centro de alumnos
  • centro de autoacceso

  • centro de estudios
  • centro de flores
  • centro de gravedad
  • centro de la nada
  • centro de mesa
  • centro de salud
  • centro de sílaba
  • centro de simetría
  • centro derecha
  • centro izquierda
  • centro penitenciario
  • centro recreativo
Related terms
[edit]
  • central
  • céntrico

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

centro

  1. first-person singular present indicative of centrar

Further reading
